fact.thing: yearly fund cost on $10,000 in Fidelity Advantage Bitcoin ETF (FBTC)
fact.claim: Fidelity Advantage Bitcoin ETF (FBTC), a Canadian spot bitcoin ETF, had an MER of 0.35% as at March 31, 2026. On $10,000 that comes to about $35 a year, taken out of the fund's value rather than billed to you, and it moves up or down with the balance. The CRA says income and capital gains earned in a TFSA are generally tax-free, even when you withdraw, as long as you stay within your contribution room. Bitcoin you sell or trade on an exchange outside a registered account may give you a capital gain (the CRA's example taxes 50% of it) or business income, and you must report it.

felt.how: 0.35% MER taken from the fund every year on a $10,000 FBTC balance

sources.what: Any contribution you make to your TFSA and any income you earn through interest, dividends or capital gains are generally tax-free, even when you make a withdrawal.

sources.label: CRA – CRYPTO-ASSET TAX OBLIGATIONS
sources.what: Based on your crypto-asset activities, you may realize business income (or loss) or capital gain (or loss).

sources.label: CRA – CALCULATING CAPITAL GAINS
sources.what: Fifty percent of the capital gain would be taxable and you would report $1,220 as your taxable capital gain on line 12700 of your 2025 Income Tax and Benefit Return.

plain.what: FBTC is a Canadian fund that holds bitcoin for you, run by Fidelity. Its yearly cost was 0.35% as at March 31, 2026, which is about $35 on $10,000, and that money comes out of the fund itself instead of arriving as a bill. The CRA says money you make inside a TFSA, a box where gains are not taxed, is generally tax free, while bitcoin you sell on an exchange outside a registered box has to be reported and can be taxed as a capital gain.
